title: Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators
description: Use BFS to find the minimum steps to move all paired items to the top floor safely.
writeup:
## Approach

This puzzle is a constrained state‑space search. Each state consists of:
- The elevator floor
- The floor of every generator
- The floor of every microchip

A state is valid only if no microchip is ever left with another generator unless its own generator is present.

The elevator can move up or down one floor, carrying one or two items. The goal is to reach a state where all items are on floor 4.

Because the search space is huge, we must:
- Use **BFS** to guarantee the shortest solution.
- Use **canonical state representations** so equivalent states collapse to the same key.
- Use **pair‑relative encoding** (chip and generator floors as tuples) to avoid treating identical items as distinct.

## Part 1

We parse the input into pairs of (generator_floor, chip_floor). We then run BFS:
- Generate all valid moves (1 or 2 items moved up/down).
- Reject invalid states (fried chips).
- Canonicalize each state to avoid duplicates.

The BFS depth at which we first reach the goal is the answer.

## Part 2

Part 2 adds four new items (two new generator/microchip pairs) on floor 1. The BFS logic is identical; only the initial state changes.

Because the state space grows, canonicalization becomes even more important. The BFS still completes in reasonable time with proper pruning.
